## What you will learn

When a population has a pedigree, haploStack can walk it generation by
generation, work out which **haplotype block each offspring inherited from each
parent**, and test which **markers reliably tag that inheritance**. This example:

1. Loads an **external pedigree file** and attaches it to a `GenoMeta`.
2. Traces the family structure (`trace_family_history()` /
   `attach_family_history()`).
3. Runs **block-level inheritance** tracing (`trace_haplotype_family()`) and
   visualises parental origins.
4. Runs **in-family IBD and marker-signal** analysis
   (`compute_block_ibd()`, `score_marker_signal()`) with its plots.

```{r load}
library(haploStack)
library(data.table)
library(ggplot2)
```

## 0  A demonstration family

We build four bi-parental families. Each offspring inherits **whole parental
blocks** (no intra-block recombination), so the inheritance signal is real and
recoverable. Founders carry random haplotypes; the pedigree is written to an
external file we read back in the next section.

```{r make-family}
set.seed(1)
alleles    <- c("1", "4")
n_per_chrom <- 6L; n_chrom <- 3L; block_size <- 3L
n_mk       <- n_per_chrom * n_chrom
markers    <- paste0("M", seq_len(n_mk))
chrom      <- rep(seq_len(n_chrom), each = n_per_chrom)
blk        <- unlist(lapply(seq_len(n_chrom),
              function(c) paste0("Chr", c, "_B", ceiling(seq_len(n_per_chrom) / block_size))))

map <- data.frame(Chrom = as.character(chrom), Marker = markers,
                  Pos = unlist(lapply(seq_len(n_chrom),
                        function(c) sort(sample(seq(1e6, 1e8, 1e5), n_per_chrom)))),
                  stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
bmm <- data.frame(Chrom = as.character(chrom), Marker = markers, Block = blk,
                  stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

# Eight founders, paired into four crosses, four offspring each.
founders <- paste0("P", 1:8)
fa <- array(NA_character_, dim = c(8L, n_mk, 2L),
            dimnames = list(founders, markers, c("1", "2")))
for (s in founders) for (h in 1:2) fa[s, , h] <- sample(alleles, n_mk, replace = TRUE)

crosses  <- data.frame(P1 = founders[c(1, 3, 5, 7)],
                       P2 = founders[c(2, 4, 6, 8)], stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
off_arr  <- list(); ped_rows <- list()
for (i in seq_len(nrow(crosses))) {
  p1 <- crosses$P1[i]; p2 <- crosses$P2[i]
  for (j in 1:4) {
    oid <- sprintf("F%d_O%d", i, j)
    oa  <- array(NA_character_, dim = c(1L, n_mk, 2L),
                 dimnames = list(oid, markers, c("1", "2")))
    for (b in unique(blk)) {
      idx <- which(blk == b)
      oa[1, idx, 1] <- fa[p1, idx, sample(2L, 1L)]   # haplotype 1 from parent 1
      oa[1, idx, 2] <- fa[p2, idx, sample(2L, 1L)]   # haplotype 2 from parent 2
    }
    off_arr[[oid]]  <- oa
    ped_rows[[oid]] <- data.frame(FID = paste0("FAM", i), IID = oid,
                                  Father = p1, Mother = p2, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  }
}

ids <- c(founders, names(off_arr))
arr <- array(NA_character_, dim = c(length(ids), n_mk, 2L),
             dimnames = list(ids, markers, c("1", "2")))
arr[founders, , ] <- fa
for (oid in names(off_arr)) arr[oid, , ] <- off_arr[[oid]]

meta <- new_geno_meta(
  geno_arrays = arr, map_info = map, block_marker_map_info = bmm,
  metadata = list(ploidy = 2L, char_dict = c("1" = 1L, "4" = 2L),
                  n_samples = length(ids), n_markers = n_mk,
                  source_format = "selectiontools", encoding = "selectiontools"))

# The pedigree: founders have missing parents ("0").
pedigree <- rbind(
  data.frame(FID = "0", IID = founders, Father = "0", Mother = "0",
             stringsAsFactors = FALSE),
  do.call(rbind, ped_rows))
rownames(pedigree) <- NULL
```

---

## 1  Load the external family-tracing file

Pedigrees usually live in a separate file (a PLINK-style FAM, or any table with
an individual-ID column and parent columns). We write ours out, then read it
back the way you would read your own.

```{r write-fam}
fam_file <- file.path(tempdir(), "pedigree.txt")
write.table(pedigree, fam_file, sep = "\t", quote = FALSE, row.names = FALSE)

# --- read your pedigree file here ---
ped_in <- read.table(fam_file, header = TRUE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
head(ped_in)
```

Attach it to the `GenoMeta`. `attach_family_history()` traces the pedigree and
stores the result at `meta$metadata$family_history`; it also stamps each
sample's birth family into `sample_info$Family`. Tell it which columns hold the
individual ID and the parents.

```{r attach}
meta <- attach_family_history(meta, ped_in,
                              parent_cols = c("Father", "Mother"),
                              id_col      = "IID")

length(meta$metadata$family_history)        # generations traced
meta$metadata$family_history[[1]][Label == "O"][1:4]   # first-generation offspring
```

> You can also trace a pedigree without a `GenoMeta` using
> `trace_family_history(ped_in, parent_cols = c("Father", "Mother"), id_col = "IID")`.

---

## 2  Block-level inheritance — `trace_haplotype_family()`

`family_history_to_pedigree()` flattens the traced history into the
`Sample / Parent1 / Parent2` form, and `trace_haplotype_family()` then assigns
each offspring haplotype-block to the parent it most resembles.

```{r trace}
ped <- family_history_to_pedigree(meta)
head(ped)

inheritance <- trace_haplotype_family(meta, ped)
head(inheritance)
```

Each row reports, for one offspring haplotype within one block, the inferred
parental origin (`Parent1`, `Parent2`, `ambiguous`, or `unknown`) and the number
of matching markers. Summarise the parental composition across all offspring:

```{r trace-viz, fig.height=4}
origin_counts <- inheritance[, .N, by = Parent][order(-N)]
origin_counts

ggplot(origin_counts, aes(x = reorder(Parent, -N), y = N, fill = Parent)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.7, show.legend = FALSE) +
  labs(x = "Inferred parental origin", y = "Offspring haplotype-blocks",
       title = "Where did offspring blocks come from?") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12)
```

---

## 3  In-family IBD and marker-signal analysis

The similarity module answers a sharper question: across a family, **which
markers reliably report that a block was inherited (IBD) from a parent?**

### 3.1  Block IBD — `compute_block_ibd()`

One row per (parental haplotype × progeny haplotype) block comparison, with the
identity-by-state similarity and the IBD call at the chosen threshold.

```{r ibd}
ibd <- compute_block_ibd(meta, threshold = 0.5)
head(ibd)
cat("Comparisons:", nrow(ibd),
    "| IBD-positive:", sum(ibd$Similarity >= 0.5), "\n")
```

### 3.2  Marker signal score — `score_marker_signal()`

For every marker, block IBD is the ground truth and per-marker allele identity
is the prediction, giving a TP/FP/TN/FN confusion table and the usual metrics
(precision, recall, F1, MCC). The `final_*` metrics down-weight
near-monomorphic markers by `MAF × (1 − MAF)`.

```{r signal}
sig <- score_marker_signal(meta, mode = "IBD")
names(sig)                                   # detail / marker / metrics / signal
head(sig$metrics[, .(Chrom, Marker, TP, FP, TN, FN, precision, recall, mcc, final_mcc)])
```

Scoring is followed by a selection: the `n` best marker(s) per block (default 1)
come back as `sig$signal`, and `attach_signal_markers()` records them on the
GenoMeta's `block_info`.

```{r signal-select}
meta <- attach_signal_markers(meta, sig$signal)
get_signal_markers(meta)
```

### 3.3  Visualise the signal markers

A Manhattan of the signal score highlights the selected markers and names the
blocks they represent…

```{r signal-manhattan, fig.height=4}
plot_marker_signal(sig$metrics, geno_meta = meta, score = "final_mcc")
```

…and a precision–recall scatter (coloured by MAF) shows which markers combine
high precision, high recall, and informative allele frequency — the markers in
the top-right are the strongest tags.

```{r signal-pr, fig.width=6, fig.height=5}
plot_signal_precision_recall(sig$metrics)
```

> Switch to `mode = "IBS"` to weight the confusion cells by block similarity
> instead of the hard IBD call — useful when inheritance is partial.

---

## Summary

| Goal | Function |
|------|----------|
| Read an external pedigree | base `read.table()` |
| Trace + attach family history | `attach_family_history()`, `trace_family_history()` |
| Flatten to a parent pedigree | `family_history_to_pedigree()` |
| Per-block parental origin | `trace_haplotype_family()` |
| Per-block IBD across a family | `compute_block_ibd()` |
| Per-marker signal test | `score_marker_signal()` |
| Signal plots | `plot_marker_signal()`, `plot_signal_precision_recall()` |
